# lua-cli

> Build, test, and deploy AI agents with custom tools, webhooks, and scheduled jobs

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/lua-cli.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lua-cli)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/lua-cli.svg)](https://github.com/lua-ai-global/lua-cli/blob/main/LICENSE)

**lua-cli** is the official command-line tool for building intelligent AI agents on the Lua platform. Create custom tools, integrate with external APIs, schedule automated tasks, and deploy to production—all from your terminal.

---

## Features

- 🤖 **LuaAgent** - Unified agent configuration with persona, skills, webhooks, and jobs
- 🛠️ **Custom Tools** - Build TypeScript tools with full type safety and Zod validation
- 🪝 **Webhooks** - HTTP endpoints for external integrations (Stripe, Shopify, etc.)
- ⏰ **Scheduled Jobs** - Cron-based and one-time background tasks
- 📥 **Preprocessors** - Filter and route messages before they reach your agent
- 📤 **Postprocessors** - Transform and format agent responses
- 🔗 **Integrations & Triggers** - Connect third-party services (Gmail, Slack, etc.) and manage event-driven triggers; pause/resume individual triggers or entire connections
- 💬 **Streaming Chat** - Real-time chat interface with typing indicators
- 🧪 **Local Testing** - Test tools, webhooks, and jobs in sandbox before deploying
- 🚀 **Batch Deployment** - Push all components with one command
- 🛒 **Marketplace** - Publish and install verified skills from the community
- 🌐 **CI/CD Ready** - Environment variable support for automated deployments

## Installation

### Global Installation (Recommended)

```bash
npm install -g lua-cli
```

### Verify Installation

```bash
lua --version
```

## Authentication

lua-cli authenticates using your API key. Get yours at [admin.heylua.ai](https://admin.heylua.ai).

The key is resolved from the following sources in priority order:

| Priority | Source                             | Use case                                                |
| -------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1        | `LUA_API_KEY` environment variable | CI/CD, Docker, server environments                      |
| 2        | `~/.lua-cli/credentials` file      | Local interactive use (written by `lua auth configure`) |
| 3        | `.env` file in project root        | Local development shorthand                             |

### Option A — Interactive setup (recommended for local dev)

```bash
lua auth configure
```

Prompts you to choose between entering an API key directly or authenticating via email OTP. Credentials are saved to `~/.lua-cli/credentials`.

```bash
# Non-interactive variants:
lua auth configure --api-key "lk_your_api_key_here"
lua auth configure --email user@example.com            # Step 1: sends OTP
lua auth configure --email user@example.com --otp 123456  # Step 2: verifies OTP
```

### Option B — Environment variable (CI/CD, Docker, servers)

Set `LUA_API_KEY` in your environment. This takes priority over all other sources and requires no file on disk — ideal for headless servers, VMs, and containers.

```bash
export LUA_API_KEY="lk_your_api_key_here"
lua push all --force --auto-deploy
```

### Option C — `.env` file (local dev shorthand)

Create a `.env` file in your project root:

```bash
echo 'LUA_API_KEY=lk_your_api_key_here' >> .env
```

lua-cli automatically loads `.env` on startup. Add `.env` to your `.gitignore` to avoid committing credentials.

### Dockerfile

Pass the key as a build argument or inject it at runtime via environment:

```dockerfile
# Inject at runtime (preferred — no key baked into image)
ENV LUA_API_KEY=${LUA_API_KEY}
RUN lua push all --force --auto-deploy
```

```bash
# Run the container with the key from your local environment:
docker run --rm -e LUA_API_KEY="$LUA_API_KEY" my-image
```

### CI/CD pipeline

**GitHub Actions:**

```yaml
- name: Deploy Agent
  run: lua push all --ci --force --auto-deploy
  env:
    LUA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LUA_API_KEY }}
```

**Generic pipeline (any CI system that supports env vars):**

```bash
export LUA_API_KEY="$LUA_API_KEY"   # already set by your CI secret manager
lua push all --ci --force --auto-deploy
```

### Logout

```bash
lua auth logout      # Removes ~/.lua-cli/credentials (prompts for confirmation)
lua auth logout --force  # No prompt
```

## Quick Start

### 1. Authenticate

```bash
lua auth configure
```

Enter your API key when prompted (get one at [admin.heylua.ai](https://admin.heylua.ai)). For CI/CD or server environments, set `LUA_API_KEY` as an environment variable instead — see [Authentication](#authentication) above.

### 2. Initialize Project

```bash
mkdir my-agent && cd my-agent
lua init
```

Follow the prompts to configure your agent.

### 3. Create a Tool

Create `src/skills/tools/WeatherTool.ts`:

```typescript
import { LuaTool } from 'lua-cli/skill';
import { z } from 'zod';

export default class WeatherTool implements LuaTool {
  name = 'get_weather';
  description = 'Get current weather for any city';

  inputSchema = z.object({
    city: z.string(),
  });

  async execute(input: z.infer<typeof this.inputSchema>) {
    return { temperature: 72, condition: 'sunny' };
  }
}
```

### 4. Test Locally

```bash
lua test      # Test individual tools
lua chat      # Interactive chat with your agent
```

### 5. Deploy to Production

```bash
lua compile
lua push all --force --auto-deploy
```

Your agent is now live! 🎉

## Core Concepts

### LuaAgent - Unified Configuration

```typescript
import { LuaAgent, LuaSkill, LuaWebhook, LuaJob } from 'lua-cli';

export const agent = new LuaAgent({
  name: 'my-assistant',
  persona: 'You are a helpful AI assistant...',
  skills: [customerSupportSkill, productSkill],
  webhooks: [paymentWebhook],
  jobs: [dailyReportJob],
});
```

### Skills - Tool Collections

```typescript
import { LuaSkill } from 'lua-cli';

export default new LuaSkill({
  name: 'weather-skill',
  description: 'Weather information tools',
  tools: [new GetWeatherTool(), new GetForecastTool()],
});
```

### Runtime APIs

Access powerful APIs in your tools:

```typescript
import { User, Products, Data, Orders } from 'lua-cli';

// User data
const user = await User.get();
await user.send([{ type: 'text', text: 'Hello!' }]);

// Products
const products = await Products.get();
await Products.create({ name: 'Widget', price: 29.99 });

// Custom data storage
await Data.create('notes', { text: 'Hello' });
const results = await Data.search('notes', 'query');
```

## Key Commands

```bash
# Project Setup
lua init                    # Initialize new project
lua compile                 # Compile TypeScript

# Development
lua test                    # Test tools interactively
lua chat                    # Chat with your agent
lua dev                     # Dev server with live reload

# Deployment
lua push                    # Push to server (interactive)
lua push all --force        # Push all without prompts
lua deploy                  # Deploy to production

# Management
lua production              # View production status
lua env                     # Manage environment variables
lua logs                    # View agent logs
lua marketplace             # Browse and install skills

# Integrations & Triggers
lua integrations list                          # List connected integrations
lua integrations connect                       # Connect a new integration (OAuth or token)
lua integrations webhooks list                 # List all triggers for an agent
lua integrations webhooks create               # Create a new trigger for a connection
lua integrations webhooks pause --webhook-id <id>          # Pause a single trigger
lua integrations webhooks resume --webhook-id <id>         # Resume a single trigger
lua integrations webhooks pause --connection-id <id>       # Pause all triggers for a connection
lua integrations webhooks resume --connection-id <id>      # Resume all triggers for a connection
lua triggers                                   # Alias for 'lua integrations webhooks'
```

## CI/CD Integration

Perfect for automated deployments. See [Authentication](#authentication) for full details on all credential methods including Dockerfiles and generic pipelines.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
- name: Deploy Agent
  run: lua push all --ci --force --auto-deploy
  env:
    LUA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LUA_API_KEY }}
```

**Global `--ci` flag**: Fails loudly on missing required flags instead of silently canceling in non-TTY environments.

## Example: E-commerce Agent

```typescript
import { LuaAgent, LuaSkill } from 'lua-cli';
import { Products, Baskets, Orders } from 'lua-cli';

const productSkill = new LuaSkill({
  name: 'product-skill',
  description: 'Product browsing and search',
  tools: [new SearchProductsTool(), new GetProductTool()],
});

const orderSkill = new LuaSkill({
  name: 'order-skill',
  description: 'Order management',
  tools: [new PlaceOrderTool(), new TrackOrderTool()],
});

export const agent = new LuaAgent({
  name: 'ecommerce-assistant',
  persona: 'You are an e-commerce assistant helping customers browse products and place orders.',
  skills: [productSkill, orderSkill],
  webhooks: [orderWebhook],
  jobs: [inventoryCheckJob],
});
```

## Sandbox Contract

lua-cli and lua-core both run user code (tools, webhooks, jobs, processors) in isolated Node.js VM sandboxes. Both sandboxes expose the same globals (User, Products, Orders, etc.) and primitive shims (LuaTool, LuaSkill, etc.) but with different backend implementations — lua-cli uses HTTP APIs for local testing, lua-core uses direct service instances in production.

To prevent these sandboxes from drifting out of sync, a **shared contract** is defined in `@lua/shared-types` (`sandbox-contract.ts`) that specifies:

- **Required primitive shims** — all class-based (LuaTool, LuaSkill, etc.) and function-based (defineTool, defineSkill, etc.) shims
- **Required platform APIs** — User, Products, Baskets, Orders, Data, Jobs, AI, CDN with their expected methods
- **Required nested APIs** — Templates.whatsapp, Lua.request
- **Required enums** — BasketStatus, OrderStatus with expected keys
- **Required utilities** — env()

Both packages run **contract compliance tests** that verify their sandbox conforms to this contract. If a new global or primitive is added to one sandbox but not the contract, CI fails.

### Updating the Contract

When adding a new sandbox global or primitive:

1. Update `packages/shared-types/src/sandbox-contract.ts` with the new entry
2. Add the global/primitive to both sandboxes:
   - lua-cli: `packages/lua-cli/src/utils/sandbox.ts`
   - lua-core: `packages/lua-core/src/mastra/common/utils/vm-execution.utils.ts`
3. Both packages' contract tests will verify the addition

## Architecture

lua-cli is part of a distributed platform:

- **lua-cli** - Developer tool (this repo)
- **lua-api** - API gateway
- **lua-agents** - Business logic service (CRUD, MongoDB)
- **lua-core** - Agent runtime (Mastra, VM sandbox, streaming)
- **lua-auth** - Authentication service
